action_key: generalization:generalize the lemma to a plain subset hypothesis, for example `lemma ismulcommutative_mono {s m : type*} [setlike s m] [mul m] [mulmemclass s m] {s t : s} (h : (s : set m) ⊆ t) [ismulcommutative t] : ismulcommutative s := .of_setlike_mul_comm fun _ ha _ hb ↦ setlike_mul_comm (h ha) (h hb)`. if you still want the order-specialized form for convenience, keep it as a thin alias on top of this more general lemma.
claim: `isMulCommutative_mono` carries unnecessary order assumptions: its proof only needs an inclusion of the underlying sets, not `[LE S] [IsConcreteLE S M]` and an order relation on `S`. As stated, the lemma is unavailable for `SetLike` subobjects without a concrete `≤` instance, even though the rest of this local API (`isMulCommutative_iff_of_setLike`, `setLike_mul_comm`) is fully `SetLike`-generic.
requested_change:
Generalize the lemma to a plain subset hypothesis, for example
`lemma isMulCommutative_mono {S M : Type*} [SetLike S M] [Mul M] [MulMemClass S M]
    {s t : S} (h : (s : Set M) ⊆ t) [IsMulCommutative t] : IsMulCommutative s :=
  .of_setLike_mul_comm fun _ ha _ hb ↦ setLike_mul_comm (h ha) (h hb)`.
If you still want the order-specialized form for convenience, keep it as a thin alias on top of this more general lemma.
